metadata.title: Random But True: The Bear Who Was Officially A Soldier
metadata.caption:
In 1942, Polish soldiers stationed in Iran traded food to a local boy for a brown bear cub. They named him Wojtek.

When British transport rules banned animals aboard the ships heading to Italy, the Polish II Corps found a way around it. They enlisted him. Wojtek was given the rank of private, a serial number and his own army paybook, which made him a documented soldier rather than a mascot.

At the battle of Monte Cassino in 1944 he carried crates of artillery shells to the gun crews. He was promoted to corporal, and his unit adopted an emblem of a bear carrying a shell as their official badge.

After the war he lived at Edinburgh Zoo until 1963.
